title: Chocolate Brownies
subtitle: Dense, fudgy dark chocolate brownies
excerpt: Dark chocolate and butter melted together with brown sugar, eggs, and a minimum of flour. Dense, fudgy, deeply chocolatey. The opposite of cakey. Set in the tin, cut cold.

recipe.sourceNotes: The brownie was invented in the United States in the late 19th century, with the first published recipe appearing in the 1906 Boston Cooking-School Cook Book. It arrived in Britain through American cookbooks and is now one of the most widely made baked goods in British homes. The distinction between fudgy and cakey brownies is a ratio question: more chocolate and butter relative to flour gives fudge; more flour gives cake. This recipe is firmly in the fudgy camp, using very little flour and relying on good dark chocolate for structure and flavour.

recipeTools.notes: A 20 x 20 cm square baking tin.

content.text: Do not over-bake: pull the brownies from the oven when a skewer in the centre still comes out with moist crumbs, not clean. Fudgy brownies look underdone when they come out of the oven. Leave to cool completely in the tin before cutting: cutting warm brownies gives a messy edge. Refrigerating for an hour before cutting gives the cleanest slices.
Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Grease and line a 20 x 20 cm tin with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a bowl over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring occasionally. Remove from the heat. Stir in the sugar. Leave to cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time. Add the vanilla. Fold in the flour, cocoa, and salt until just combined.

Pour into the prepared tin. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until the top is set but a skewer still comes out with moist crumbs. Cool completely in the tin. Refrigerate for 1 hour before cutting into 16 squares.
